name: Grumman HU-16 Albatross
summary: Large twin-engine amphibious flying boat used for air-sea rescue by the USAF, USN and USCG; a small fleet of privately owned examples remains in flight.

wings: High, straight wing mounted on top of the fuselage
engines: Two R-1820 radial engines on the wing leading edge
fuselage: Boat hull with a step and a high pilot canopy
Retractable main gear folding into the hull
Large nose with a radome on some versions
tail: Tall fin with a high-mounted horizontal tail (T-tail)

tellTales: Large twin-radial amphibian flying boat with wingtip floats
High wing on a boat hull with a tall T-tail
Big, deep hull with retractable wheels

confusedWith.howToTell: The Mallard is smaller with a conventional low tail and engines in the wing; the Albatross is much larger with a T-tail.
The Goose is much smaller with a conventional tail; the Albatross is larger with a T-tail.
The Tracker has a conventional fuselage; the Albatross has a boat hull and wingtip floats.
The DC-3 has no hull or floats; the Albatross is an amphibian.
